title: 序第一章黑木涯分别一
content_zh:
长安的上元夜，总带着一股子让人心尖发暖的热闹。
朱雀大街上，灯笼从街头挂到街尾，绣着鸾鸟、麒麟的纱灯被晚风托着轻轻晃，光透过薄纱洒在青石板路上，晕出一片朦胧的暖黄。街边小贩的吆喝声此起彼伏，糖画师傅手腕一转，一只栩栩如生的糖龙便落在石板上，引得孩童围着拍手；卖花灯的摊子前，姑娘们挑着兔子灯、荷花灯，笑靥比灯影还亮。
城南，青藤巷。
与大街上的喧嚣不同，这里静得能听见巷口老槐树的叶子簌簌落。巷尾那座青砖灰瓦的小院，便是萧书生的住处。院门上没有匾额，只在门楣边爬着几丛牵牛花，此刻花瓣已收，只剩墨绿的藤蔓缠着木门，倒添了几分清幽。
屋内，烛火摇曳。
萧书生坐在案前，手里握着一支狼毫笔，笔尖悬在宣纸上，却迟迟没有落下。案上摊着一卷《论语》，旁边放着半盏早已凉透的茶。他穿着一身洗得发白的青布长衫，头发用一根木簪随意束着，侧脸的轮廓在烛光下显得有些清瘦，唯有那双眼睛，亮得像藏着星光，只是此刻，那星光里蒙着一层淡淡的愁绪。
他不是不想写，只是方才整理旧书时，从一本泛黄的《昭明文选》里，掉出了一样东西——一本巴掌大的密卷。
密卷的纸是极少见的蚕丝纸，摸起来细腻光滑，却已泛出深黄，边缘有些磨损，像是被人反复摩挲过。最让萧书生心头一紧的是，密卷的边角处，沾着一点暗红的印记，那颜色，像极了干涸的血迹。
他小心翼翼地展开密卷，里面的字迹是用朱砂写的，笔画遒劲有力，却因年代久远，有些模糊。萧书生凑近烛火，逐字辨认，越看，手指便攥得越紧，指节泛出青白。
密卷里记的，竟是前朝宝藏的线索。
更让他心惊的是，文中还提到了一个名字——林墨尘。
那是他的恩师。
十年前，林墨尘还是朝中有名的文臣，为人正直，却突然以“通敌叛国”的罪名被打入天牢，没过多久，便传来了“病逝”的消息。当时萧书生刚及弱冠，得知消息后，疯了似的闯宫门、求权贵，却连恩师的最后一面都没见到。后来他才从一位老狱卒口中得知，林墨尘根本不是病逝，而是在牢中被人暗害，死前还曾试图将一卷东西送出，却不知下落。
那时的萧书生，悲愤交加，却无能为力。他只能带着恩师留下的一支竹笔、一柄长剑，离开京城，浪迹江湖。直到三年前，才悄悄回到长安，隐在这青藤巷里，靠抄书为生，只盼着能过上几天安稳日子。
可如今，这密卷的出现，却像一块石头，投进了他平静的心湖，激起千层浪。
他看着密卷上“林墨尘”三个字，眼眶微微发热。十年了，恩师的模样还清晰地印在他脑海里——那年他初入师门，因家境贫寒，连一件像样的长衫都没有，是恩师把自己的旧衣改了给他穿；他读书犯困，是恩师用戒尺轻轻敲他的手心，却又端来温热的莲子羹；他第一次握剑，手抖得厉害，是恩师握着他的手，教他出剑、收剑，说“剑可护己，亦可护人，更要护心中道义”。
恩师一生清廉，怎么可能“通敌叛国”？这密卷，会不会就是恩师当年想送出的东西？那宝藏线索背后，又藏着怎样的秘密？恩师的死，到底是谁一手策划的？
无数个疑问，在萧书生的脑海里翻腾。他站起身，走到窗边，推开窗户。巷子里静悄悄的，只有远处大街上的喧闹声隐约传来，衬得这小院愈发冷清。
夜风带着一丝凉意，吹在他脸上，让他纷乱的心绪稍稍平静了些。他知道，这密卷一旦现世，必定会引来无数觊觎。江湖上的门派、朝廷里的权贵，谁不想要前朝宝藏？而他，一个只想安稳度日的“废人”，又怎能守住这烫手山芋？
可他又不能不管。那是恩师的冤屈，是十年未解的谜团。如果连他都放弃了，恩师在九泉之下，又怎能安息？

萧书生低头，看了看自己的双手。这双手，曾经握剑，也曾经握笔。握剑时，他能斩奸除恶，护一方安宁；握笔时，他能写尽江湖，道人间不平。只是这几年，他刻意让这双手只沾墨，不沾血，可现在，他知道，有些事，躲不过，也不能躲。
他转身回到案前，将密卷小心地收好，放进贴身的衣袋里。然后，他拿起案上的长剑——那是恩师当年送他的，剑鞘已经有些陈旧，却依旧透着一股凛然的剑气。他轻轻拔出剑，月光透过窗户洒在剑身上，映出一片冷冽的寒光。
剑未生锈，他的手，也未生疏。
萧书生握紧长剑，目光变得坚定。他知道，从捡到密卷的那一刻起，他平静的日子，就结束了。接下来，他要面对的，是江湖的风波，是朝廷的暗斗，是未知的危险。可他不怕，因为他的心里，还记着恩师的话——“护心中道义”。
窗外，灯笼的光依旧明亮，可萧书生知道，这长安的热闹背后，早已暗流涌动。而他，萧书生，将再次拿起剑与笔，踏入这风波之中，为恩师洗冤，为道义而战。
夜，还很长。但萧书生知道，属于他的故事，才刚刚开始。

content_en:
The Shangyuan Night in Chang'an always brings a heart-warming excitement.
On Zhuque Street, lanterns are hung from the street to the end of the street. The gauze lanterns embroidered with Luan birds and unicorns are gently swayed by the evening breeze. The light shines through the gauze on the bluestone road, creating a hazy warm yellow. Street vendors shouted loudly, and with a twist of the sugar painter's wrist, a lifelike sugar dragon landed on the stone slab, attracting children to crowd around and clap their hands. In front of the stall selling lanterns, girls carried rabbit lanterns and lotus lanterns, their smiles brighter than the shadows of the lamps.
In the south of the city, Ivy Lane.
Different from the hustle and bustle on the street, it is so quiet here that you can hear the leaves of the old locust trees falling in the alley. The small courtyard with green bricks and gray tiles at the end of the alley is the residence of Scholar Xiao. There is no plaque on the courtyard door, only a few clusters of morning glories crawling beside the lintel. The petals have been closed at this moment, leaving only dark green vines wrapped around the wooden door, adding a bit of tranquility.
Inside the house, candlelight flickered.
Scholar Xiao was sitting in front of the case, holding a langhao pen in his hand. The tip of the pen was hanging on the rice paper, but it did not fall down. A volume of "The Analects of Confucius" is spread out on the table, and next to it is half a cup of tea that has already cooled down. He was wearing a green cloth gown that had been washed white, and his hair was tied up casually with a wooden hairpin. The profile of his face looked a little thin under the candlelight, but his eyes were as bright as hiding stars, but at this moment, the stars were covered with a faint layer of melancholy.
It's not that he doesn't want to write, it's just that when he was sorting out old books, something fell out from a yellowed "Selected Works of Zhaoming" - a palm-sized secret volume.
The densely rolled paper is a rare silk paper. It feels delicate and smooth, but it has turned dark yellow and has some wear and tear on the edges, as if it has been rubbed repeatedly. What worries Scholar Xiao the most is that there is a dark red mark on the corner of the dense volume. The color is very much like dried blood.
He carefully unfolded the secret scroll. The writing inside was written in cinnabar. The strokes were strong and powerful, but they were a little blurry due to the age. Scholar Xiao leaned closer to the candlelight and read each word. The more he read, the tighter his fingers clenched and his knuckles turned blue and white.
What was written in the secret volume was actually a clue to the treasure of the previous dynasty.
What shocked him even more was that a name was mentioned in the article - Lin Mochen.
That was his mentor.
Ten years ago, Lin Mochen was a well-known civil servant in the court and an upright man. However, he was suddenly thrown into a prison for "collaborating with the enemy and treason." Not long after, the news came that he had "died of illness." At that time, Scholar Xiao had just reached the throne. After learning the news, he rushed into the palace like crazy to seek power, but he did not even see his mentor for the last time. Later, he learned from an old jailer that Lin Mochen did not die of illness at all, but was assassinated in prison. Before his death, he tried to give away a roll of stuff, but his whereabouts were unknown.
At that time, Scholar Xiao was filled with grief and anger, but was powerless. He could only leave the capital and wander around the world with a bamboo pen and a long sword left by his mentor. It wasn't until three years ago that I quietly returned to Chang'an, hiding in Ivy Lane, making a living by copying books, hoping to live a stable life for a few days.
But now, the appearance of this secret scroll was like a stone thrown into the calm lake of his heart, stirring up a thousand waves.
He looked at the words "Lin Mochen" on the secret scroll, his eyes burning slightly. Ten years later, the image of his mentor was still clearly imprinted in his mind - that year when he first entered the teacher's school, his family was poor and he didn't even have a decent gown, so his mentor altered his own old clothes and gave them to him to wear; he was sleepy while studying, so it was his mentor who used The ruler gently tapped his palm, but he was brought warm lotus seed soup. It was the first time he held a sword, and his hand shook violently. It was his mentor who held his hand and taught him how to draw and sheath the sword, saying, "A sword can protect yourself and others, and more importantly, it must protect the moral principles in your heart."
How could his mentor "collaborate with the enemy and treason" if his life was clean and honest? Could this secret scroll be what the teacher wanted to give back then? What kind of secrets are hidden behind the treasure clues? Who planned the death of his mentor?
Countless questions, in XiaoThe scholar's mind was churning. He stood up, walked to the window, and opened it. The alley was quiet, only the noise from the street in the distance could be heard faintly, making the small courtyard even more deserted.
The night breeze blew a bit of coolness on his face, calming his chaotic mind a little. He knew that once this secret scroll appeared in the world, it would definitely attract countless covetous people. Among the sects in the world and the dignitaries in the court, who doesn’t want the treasures of the previous dynasty? And how could he, a "waste" who just wanted to live a stable life, hold on to this hot potato?
But he couldn't ignore it. That was the injustice of my mentor, and it was a mystery that remained unsolved for ten years. If even he gave up, how could his mentor rest in peace even if he was under the Nine Springs?
Scholar Xiao lowered his head and looked at his hands. These hands once held swords and pens. When holding a sword, he can kill evil and protect peace; when holding a pen, he can write about all the rivers and lakes and speak out about injustice in the world. It's just that in the past few years, he deliberately let his hands be stained only with ink and not with blood, but now, he knows that there are some things that cannot be avoided and cannot be avoided.
He turned back to the case, carefully put the secret volume away, and put it into his close-fitting pocket. Then, he picked up the long sword on the table - it was given to him by his mentor back then. The scabbard was a little old, but it still exuded an awe-inspiring sword aura. He gently pulled out the sword, and the moonlight shone on the sword through the window, reflecting a cold light.
The sword is not rusty, and his hands are not rusty either.
Scholar Xiao clenched his sword tightly and his eyes became firm. He knew that from the moment he picked up the secret scroll, his peaceful days were over. Next, what he has to face is the turmoil in the world, the secret struggle in the court, and the unknown danger. But he is not afraid, because he still remembers his mentor's words in his heart - "Protect the morality in your heart."
Outside the window, the light of the lantern was still bright, but Shusheng Xiao knew that behind the bustle of Chang'an, there was already an undercurrent surging. And he, Scholar Xiao, will pick up his sword and pen again and step into this turmoil to clear his mentor's wrongdoing and fight for morality.
The night is still very long. But Shusheng Xiao knew that his story had just begun.
